issues.description: Problem statement UML specifies `Stock.add(String): void`, but both template and solution declare `add(String)` as returning `int` (returning updated quantity or -1). This inconsistency makes it unclear what method signature students should implement and what tests will compile against, especially since `Stock.take(String)` is explicitly shown as returning `int` in the UML.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the UML/spec with the code by changing the diagram entry to `+add(String): int` (optionally documenting that it returns the new quantity or -1). Alternatively, change both template and solution to `void add(String)` and update all call sites accordingly.

issues.description: Problem statement UML for `Stock` lists only operational methods and implies `stockIngredients` is managed internally, but template and solution expose a public mutator `setStockIngredients(StockIngredient[])`. This extra public API can mislead students about required encapsulation and what methods are expected/allowed by the specification.
issues.suggestedFix: Either update the UML/spec to explicitly include `setStockIngredients(StockIngredient[])` (and possibly `getStockIngredients()`), or remove `setStockIngredients` from template/solution and rely on `addToStockIngredients(...)`/`emptyStock()` for controlled mutation.

issues.description: Text requires `SealSaloon.stock` to be static and shared across instances, but the UML association `SealSaloon -> Stock : stock` does not indicate static/shared semantics and looks like an instance field. This can confuse students about whether stock is per-saloon or global.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify static/shared nature in the UML/statement (e.g., mark attribute as `{static}` or add a note near the association/attribute) so the diagram matches the text and reference implementation.
